h: Inside the bunker: what to look out for
p: Some of the smaller rooms are just as fascinating as the famous ones. Keep an eye out for Churchill's bedroom, a modest space for a man running a war, and the Transatlantic Telephone Room, disguised as a private toilet, where secret calls could be made to the President of the United States. Little touches like these really bring home how much secrecy surrounded the place.

Allow a couple of hours to see everything properly. The bunker and the Churchill Museum together hold a lot of detail, and reading the stories and listening to recordings takes time. It's a popular attraction, so going early in the day or later in the afternoon can feel calmer, especially during school holidays.
Space can feel tight in places, which is part of the atmosphere but worth knowing if anyone in your group isn't keen on enclosed spaces. The rooms were built for function, not comfort, after all.

The location is perfect for building a full day of sightseeing around Westminster. Westminster and St James's Park Tube stations are both within walking distance. Afterwards, walk up Whitehall past the Cenotaph and the gates of Downing Street, stop by Horse Guards Parade, then carry on to Trafalgar Square and the National Gallery.

Prefer some green space? St James's Park is right next door, with its lake, pelicans and views towards Buckingham Palace. Westminster Abbey is a short stroll the other way, so you can easily pair two of London's most historic sites in a single day.
